# Pandamonium v1.0.52

This release ships the full built-in tool catalog for the agent plus a small sidebar polish pass.

Agent turns now mount every enabled built-in tool, `manage_settings list_tools` reports the real catalog, and `load_tools` mounts any tool on demand for the remainder of a request. In the sidebar, bucket headers are flush left again at rest — the drag handle reveals itself only on hover and slides the label aside instead of permanently reserving a column — and the Projects section no longer prints instruction text under its header when it is empty.

## MAD-905 + MAD-907 — Agent: full built-in tool catalog and on-demand mounting

### Problem

The Built-in Tools panel catalogs 80 tools, but API turns mounted only the RAG-selected subset (a live session showed 23 of 80), `manage_settings list_tools` returned a hardcoded summary instead of the catalog, and local/text engines never received most of the catalog at all. The agent could not invoke two-thirds of its own tools and often concluded a tool was missing.

### Implementation

API-host engines mount every enabled built-in schema each round; per-turn intent clamps stay authoritative and the measured tool-catalog budget (`cap_tool_schemas`) is the only trim. `manage_settings action=list_tools` returns the real catalog with id, category, description, and enabled state. `action=load_tools` mounts any enabled built-in for the remainder of the request and returns its exact fenced-block usage so text/local engines can format the call immediately; mounted tools rank ahead of the budget cap, and the discovery gateway is always available (network-inspection turns stay allowlisted). `generate_image` and `manage_research` gained native schemas and `tail_serve_output` a toggle, closing the catalog/callable parity drift.

### Product value and UI visibility

No UI change. Every tool the Built-in Tools panel lists as enabled is now actually callable by the agent, and "how many tools do you have?" is answered from live state.

### Verification

`tests/test_agent_tool_catalog_uncap.py` and `tests/test_tool_catalog_mount.py` cover full API mounting, disabled-tool respect, intent-clamp preservation, the real catalog listing, load/mount validation, and budget-cap recovery; 441 focused regression tests pass alongside catalog parity, workspace confine, context manifest, and network routing checks.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No new dependency or configuration. Mounts last for the current request only.

## MAD-908 — UI: keep bucket headers flush and drop the Projects empty-state copy

### Problem

The bucket drag handle introduced with section reordering occupied layout space even while invisible. Every sidebar section icon and label was pushed right by the reserved handle column, which read as a misalignment against the rest of the sidebar. Separately, an empty Projects section rendered an instruction sentence under the header that cluttered the list.

### Implementation

The handle is now absolutely positioned inside the section header, contributes no layout width, and is pointer-transparent at rest so it cannot intercept a click meant for the section title. Hovering or keyboard-focusing a header reveals the handle and transitions the label right by the handle width; leaving restores it. Rearrange mode keeps the shifted layout so the handle never overlaps the label. The Projects empty-state element and its render/error copy were removed; an empty section shows only its header and the add control.

### Product value and UI visibility

Sidebar icons and labels line up exactly as they did before reordering was added. The affordance is discoverable on hover without permanently costing alignment, and the Projects list is quiet when empty.

### Verification

`tests/test_bucket_header_flush.py` guards the overlay positioning, the hover slide, the pointer-events behavior, and the removed empty-state markup. The browser check in `tests/browser/mad-899-ui-batch.spec.js` measures the label position at rest versus on hover, asserts the handle opacity transition, and asserts no `#projects-empty` element exists.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend-only CSS/markup/JS change with no data, schema, or API impact. Touch layouts already hid the handle and are unchanged. No new dependency.
